install.heading: Installation
install.intro: How to install the app, connect the DS2000 and update the firmware. It takes about five minutes.

app_steps.title: Download the installer
app_steps.body: Get the .msi file from the Downloads tab.

app_steps.title: Get past SmartScreen
app_steps.body: The installer is not signed yet, so Windows warns the first time. Click More info.
app_steps.alt: Windows SmartScreen warning with the More info link

app_steps.title: Run it anyway
app_steps.body: A Run anyway button appears. Click it and follow the installer.
app_steps.alt: SmartScreen warning with the Run anyway button

app_steps.title: Open DS2000
app_steps.body: The app lives in the system tray, next to the clock. Clicking the icon opens the window; closing the window does not quit the app. To quit, right-click the icon and choose Quit.
app_steps.alt: DS2000 icon in the system tray with its menu

device_steps.title: Plug it in over USB
device_steps.body: The app finds it on its own. No drivers are needed: Windows sees it as a serial port.

device_steps.title: Check the status
device_steps.body: In the Settings tab, the Connections section must read Serial: Connected. If it says the firmware is out of date, update it as described below.
device_steps.alt: The app's Settings tab showing Serial: Connected

device_steps.title: Connect Discord
device_steps.body: One more step, done once: create your Discord application. It is explained in the Discord setup tab.

install.firmware_intro: Only needed when the app says the firmware is out of date. The app will do this on its own in the future.

firmware_steps.title: Download the image
firmware_steps.body: In Downloads, get the .uf2 file for your board.

firmware_steps.title: Enter upload mode
firmware_steps.body: Quit the DS2000 app. Unplug the device, hold the board's BOOT button and plug it back in. A USB drive called RP2350 appears (RPI-RP2 on a Pico).
firmware_steps.alt: Windows Explorer showing the RP2350 drive

firmware_steps.title: Copy the file
firmware_steps.body: Drag the .uf2 onto that drive. The board restarts with the new firmware and the drive disappears. Open the app again.

install.uninstall_body: From Windows Settings → Apps. The settings stay in %APPDATA%\Mechardo and the Discord credentials in Windows Credential Manager, under DS2000; delete them by hand if you are not reinstalling.

discord.heading: Discord setup
discord.intro: Discord only lets an application control your microphone if you own that application. That is why DS2000 does not ship one: you create your own in Discord's developer portal. It is free, done once, and needs no programming.
before: The Discord desktop app open and signed in.
A browser to open the developer portal.

portal_steps.title: Open the developer portal
portal_steps.body: Go to discord.com/developers/applications with your Discord account and click New Application, top right.
portal_steps.alt: Discord developer portal with the New Application button

portal_steps.title: Name it
portal_steps.body: Any name works, for example DS2000. Accept Discord's terms and click Create.
portal_steps.alt: Create an application dialog with the name DS2000

portal_steps.title: Copy the Client ID
portal_steps.body: In the left menu, open OAuth2. Copy the Client ID with the Copy button and keep it for the last step.
portal_steps.alt: OAuth2 page with the Client ID and the Copy button

portal_steps.title: Generate the Client Secret
portal_steps.body: On the same page, click Reset Secret and confirm. Discord may ask for your two-factor code. Copy the secret: Discord shows it only once. If you lose it, generate another. Do not share it with anyone.
portal_steps.alt: A freshly generated Client Secret, blurred, with the Copy button

portal_steps.title: Add the redirect
portal_steps.body: Further down, under Redirects, click Add Redirect, type exactly http://localhost/ (with the trailing slash) and click Save Changes. Without it the connection fails.
portal_steps.alt: Redirects section with http://localhost/ entered and the Save Changes button

app_steps.title: Paste the credentials
app_steps.body: In DS2000, open the Discord tab, paste the Client ID and the Client Secret, and click Connect.
app_steps.alt: The DS2000 app's Discord tab with both fields filled in

app_steps.title: Authorise in Discord
app_steps.body: Discord shows an authorisation request with your application's name. Click Authorize.
app_steps.alt: Discord authorisation request for the DS2000 application

app_steps.title: Done
app_steps.body: The Discord tab reads Connected to Discord., and Settings → Connections reads Discord: Connected. Try the keys: mute, deafen and disconnect. The credentials are saved, so this is not repeated.
app_steps.alt: The DS2000 app showing Discord: Connected

trouble.q: It stays on “Credentials saved. Waiting for Discord…”
trouble.a: The Discord desktop app has to be running. Open it; DS2000 connects on its own within a few seconds.

trouble.q: I accepted the authorisation but it does not connect
trouble.a: Check that Redirects holds exactly http://localhost/, with the trailing slash, and that the changes were saved.
Generate another with Reset Secret and paste the new one in DS2000's Discord tab. Leaving the field empty keeps the old one.

trouble.q: I want to unlink the application
trouble.a: In DS2000's Discord tab, Unlink deletes the saved credentials. To delete the application as well, remove it from the developer portal.

discord.privacy: The Client Secret and the tokens are stored in Windows Credential Manager, on your computer. They are sent to nobody but Discord, and never to Mechardo Labs.

source.heading: Open source
source.intro: All of the DS2000 is open: the app, the firmware, the board and the enclosure. Each part has its own GitHub repository.

app.name: DS2000
app.desc: Windows desktop app: the Discord link, device detection and the lighting controls.

firmware.name: DS2000-Firmware
firmware.desc: Device firmware: reads the keys, drives the LEDs and talks to the app over USB.

pcb.name: DS2000-PCB
pcb.desc: Schematic and board layout, with the RP2350A and Kailh Choc switches.

enclosure.name: DS2000-Enclosure
enclosure.desc: 3D-printed enclosure: the model, print-ready exports and print settings.

source.protocol: Serial protocol between the app and the firmware
source.contribute: Issues and pull requests are welcome. Each repository's README explains how to build it.
